Implement the Boot-based ModuleRunner (U8) on top of Spring Boot 3.x for container-managed execution.
Apply the Service Provider Interface (SPI) pattern using java.util.ServiceLoader for the pluggable module deployment runtime (U7).
Use JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness) for the TupleBuilder (U5) and jdbchdfs (U4) benchmark suites to obtain statistically sound results.
Adopt Gradle as the build system, adding an explicit 'install' target wired into the CI pipeline (U2).
Parameter escaping for GPDB/SQLServer (U6) will be handled at the JDBC option-builder layer so callers no longer need to pre-escape values.
Publish the XD + Kafka POC (U3) to the existing 'samples' repository with a README and a runnable docker-compose for verification.
Treat module deployment migration (U7) as backward-compatible: existing repository-based deployments continue to work via a default SPI implementation.
assumptions: A single experienced developer familiar with the Spring XD codebase performs all the work end-to-end.
Effort values are focused development hours (coding, debugging, reviewing, basic verification) and exclude meetings and time off.
The DEBS challenge work (U1) represents the remaining, well-scoped portion of an already in-progress solution, not the full challenge from scratch.
A working development environment, IDE, JDK 17, and Gradle wrapper are already available on the developer's machine.
CI infrastructure (e.g., Jenkins) already exists; the work for U2 only adds a new job plus the install target configuration.
Unit, integration, and performance test infrastructure is already in place; new tests integrate with these existing harnesses.
Documentation templates, the 'samples' repository access, and publishing workflow are all established and require only content creation.
No major upstream API changes or cross-team coordination are needed beyond the scope expressed in the user stories.
GPDB and SQLServer test databases are available (locally or in test containers) for the Sqoop UX comparison (U6).
The 'container-managed environments' referenced in U8 assume standard OCI-compatible runtimes (e.g., Docker/Kubernetes).
